issue: Can a defendant bring a constitutional claim (under the Sixth Amendment speedy-trial right or the Fourteenth Amendment's Due Process Clause) based on unreasonable delay between conviction and sentencing?
provision: U.S. Const. amend. VI; U.S. Const. amend. XIV (Due Process Clause)

sides.position: Pre-sentencing delay may support a constitutional claim analyzed under the Sixth Amendment speedy-trial framework (Barker v. Wingo factors) applied to sentencing
cases: United States v. Abou-Kassem, 78 F.3d 161 (5th Cir. 1996)
United States v. Yelverton, 197 F.3d 531 (D.C. Cir. 1999)

sides.position: Pre-sentencing delay may support a claim under a due-process framework under the Fourteenth Amendment
cases: United States v. Sanders, 452 F.3d 572 (6th Cir. 2006)

quote: But these cases were not controlling; did not reflect a single unified framework; and largely relied on the Sixth Amendment's Speedy Trial Clause, not the Fourteenth Amendment's Due Process Clause.
cite: Carman Deck v. Richard Jennings, 978 F.3d 578 (8th Cir. 2020)
